title: Bayes' Rule
prompt: A disease affects 1% of people. A test is 90% sensitive (P(+|D) = 9/10) with a 10% false-positive rate (P(+|¬D) = 1/10). Given a positive test, find P(D|+) as an exact fraction.
hint: P(D|+) = P(+|D)P(D) / P(+); the base rate dominates
recap:
Bayes' rule inverts conditionals: P(D|+) = P(+|D)·P(D) / P(+), with P(+) = P(+|D)P(D) + P(+|¬D)P(¬D). A low base rate makes most positives false — the base-rate fallacy.

Example — P(D)=0.01, P(+|D)=0.9, P(+|¬D)=0.1: P(+) = 0.009 + 0.099 = 0.108, so P(D|+) = 0.009/0.108 = 1/12 ≈ 8%.

Reference: Blitzstein & Hwang, Introduction to Probability, ch. 2.
